2019.Q1:
### Financial Insights

1. **Nucor's consolidated net earnings rose 42% year-over-year to \$501.8 million in 2019Q1, supported by a 9% increase in net sales to \$6.10 billion.**  
   Compared to 2018Q1 net earnings of \$354.2 million and net sales of \$5.57 billion, Nucor improved its net earnings margin to 8.2% from 6.4%. Earnings per diluted share increased from \$1.10 to \$1.63. The year-over-year sales increase was driven by a 13% rise in average sales price per ton (from \$799 to \$901), despite a 3% decline in shipments to external customers (6.77 million tons vs. 6.97 million tons). The 2019Q1 results included a \$33.7 million gain from the sale of an equity method investment in the raw materials segment, contributing \$0.08 per diluted share. [8-K 2019-04-23; 10-Q 2019-05-08]

2. **Operating rates at steel mills declined to 87% in 2019Q1 from 92% in 2018Q1, reflecting a 4% decrease in steel mill shipments and continued margin pressure on sheet products.**  
   Steel mill shipments to outside customers fell 5% to 4.77 million tons (from 5.02 million tons in 2018Q1), with sheet shipments down 2% and bars down 11%. Management attributed the decline primarily to lower average selling prices and metal margins for sheet products, as customers aggressively managed inventories amid a declining scrap price environment and new domestic capacity. The overall steel mills segment earnings before income taxes increased from \$560.5 million in 2018Q1 to \$689.4 million in 2019Q1 but decreased sequentially from Q4 2018 due to margin compression. [8-K 2019-04-23; 10-Q 2019-05-08]

3. **Raw materials segment earnings decreased in 2019Q1 compared to 2018Q1 and sequentially, driven by margin compression in direct reduced iron (DRI) operations and scrap processing.**  
   Net sales for raw materials dropped 5% year-over-year to \$492.7 million, primarily due to lower average selling prices at DJJ's brokerage operations despite increased volumes. The DRI businesses in Trinidad and Louisiana faced declining average selling prices since 2018Q4 and increased iron ore costs, compressing margins. The segment’s earnings before income taxes declined from \$74.5 million in 2018Q1 to \$53.2 million in 2019Q1. The gain on sale of an equity method investment partially offset these decreases. [10-Q 2019-05-08; 8-K 2019-04-23]

4. **Nucor maintained strong liquidity with \$1.6 billion in cash and cash equivalents as of March 30, 2019, and continued its share repurchase program, buying back 1.2 million shares at an average price of \$60.69.**  
   The company had approximately \$1.4 billion available under its share repurchase authorization at quarter-end. Interest expense net of income was \$28.4 million in 2019Q1, down from \$37.1 million in 2018Q1, reflecting lower debt costs or balances. The Board declared a \$0.40 quarterly dividend, the 184th consecutive quarterly dividend. Capital expenditures for 2019 were projected at approximately \$1.8 billion, up from \$997 million in 2018, driven by multiple expansion projects including a new plate mill. [8-K 2019-04-23; 10-Q 2019-05-08]

### Operations Insights

5. **Total steel shipments decreased 4% year-over-year to 5.99 million tons in 2019Q1, with the largest shipment declines in bars (-11%) and structural products (-6%), partially offset by a 2% increase in plate shipments.**  
   Shipments to outside customers in the steel products segment fell 3% to 6.77 million tons. Some downstream businesses such as piling (+10%) and other categories (+9%) showed shipment growth. The steel mills operated at 87% capacity utilization, down from 92% in 2018Q1, reflecting softer demand and inventory management by customers. Unusually challenging winter weather delayed shipments to certain nonresidential construction customers, exacerbating typical seasonal softness. [8-K 2019-04-23; 10-Q 2019-05-08]

6. **Raw materials segment utilization declined to 71% in 2019Q1 from 74% in 2018Q1, aligned with margin pressures and lower scrap flow into DJJ’s yards.**  
   The scrap processing operations saw margin compression per unit and a decline in scrap volume compared to 2018Q1. Nucor’s DRI facilities faced input cost pressures from rising iron ore costs and falling product prices. The company uses DRI to provide operational flexibility when prime scrap prices increase, but in this period, DRI margins were under pressure. [10-Q 2019-05-08]

7. **Nucor announced a new steel plate mill project in Brandenburg, Kentucky, with estimated annual capacity of 1.2 million tons and approximately 400 employees, expected to be operational in 2022.**  
   This greenfield project will complement existing plate mills in North Carolina, Alabama, and Texas, enabling production of about 97% of the domestic plate market products, including specialty higher-margin items. The project is part of a broader capital expenditure increase in 2019 aimed at expanding capacity and product offerings. [8-K 2019-04-23; 10-Q 2019-05-08]

### Commercial Strategy Insights

8. **Average sales price per ton increased 13% year-over-year to \$901 in 2019Q1, but decreased 4% sequentially from 2018Q4, reflecting weakening sheet product prices and margin compression.**  
   Management reported that sheet mill customers were aggressively managing inventories due to higher end-2018 inventory levels, declining scrap prices, and new capacity. Margins for sheet products and plate were expected to weaken further in 2019Q2, offset by improving margins in structural and bar products. The steel products segment saw earnings decreases in tubular products and rebar fabrication but improvements in building systems, joist, and deck operations. [8-K 2019-04-23; 10-Q 2019-05-08]

9. **The steel products segment’s earnings before income taxes declined year-over-year to \$77.4 million in 2019Q1 from \$85.8 million in 2018Q1 due to weaker tubular and cold-finished steel businesses, despite growth in piling and joist/deck products.**  
   Shipments of tubular products and cold finished steel declined 7% and 3%, respectively, while piling shipments increased 10%. The segment’s profitability was negatively impacted by seasonal softness and challenging winter weather delaying construction-related shipments. Management expects significant improvement in steel products segment earnings in 2019Q2 due to typical seasonal patterns and improved weather. [10-Q 2019-05-08; 8-K 2019-04-23]

### Corporate and Risk Insights

10. **Nucor identified key enterprise risks including competitive pressure on sales and pricing, trade policies, raw material and energy cost volatility, and market demand fluctuations.**  
    The company indicated that prevailing steel prices and raw material costs (notably scrap steel) materially affect operating results, with a time lag in passing through cost changes to customers. Nucor uses derivative instruments to hedge exposure to natural gas and metal prices, with accumulated other comprehensive losses of \$6.5 million at quarter-end related to these derivatives. The company’s conservative financial practices and strong credit ratings (S&P A-, Moody’s Baa1) underpin liquidity and capital deployment flexibility. [8-K 2019-04-23; 10-Q 2019-05-08]

11. **Nucor’s effective tax rate impact included a \$21.8 million deferred tax asset write-off in 2018Q1 related to a subsidiary’s tax status change; no similar charge occurred in 2019Q1.**  
    The company reclassified stranded tax effects from accumulated other comprehensive income to retained earnings effective January 1, 2019, per new accounting guidance, with no material impact on consolidated financials. Nucor’s tax positions remain under examination by various jurisdictions, including Canada and multiple U.S. states. [10-Q 2019-05-08]

### Wrap Up

In 2019Q1, Nucor reported a substantial year-over-year earnings increase driven mainly by higher steel prices despite a modest decline in shipments and operating rates. The steel mills segment saw margin pressures on sheet products, while plate, bar, and structural mills contributed positively. The raw materials segment faced margin compression in DRI and scrap processing, partially offset by a one-time gain on an equity investment sale. The company maintained strong liquidity, continued share repurchases, and declared a quarterly dividend.

Operationally, shipment declines in bars and structural products contrasted with growth in plate and piling. Weather disruptions and seasonal softness constrained steel product shipments and margins, though improved conditions were anticipated for 2019Q2. Capital expenditures are set to nearly double in 2019, reflecting multiple expansion projects including a new plate mill expected online in 2022. Nucor’s risk disclosures highlight sensitivity to raw material pricing, trade policies, and market demand, with active hedging and conservative financial management supporting resilience.

**Guidance Overview:**  
For 2019Q2, Nucor expects earnings to be similar to 2019Q1 excluding the \$33.7 million gain on the equity investment sale. Steel mill segment margins for sheet and plate products are projected to weaken further but should be offset by improving margins in structural and bar mill products. The steel products segment anticipates significant earnings improvement due to seasonal demand recovery and better weather. The raw materials segment’s profitability is expected to decline further due to ongoing margin compression in DRI operations. [8-K 2019-04-23; 10-Q 2019-05-08]
2019.Q2:
### Financial Insights

1. **Nucor’s net sales declined 9% year-over-year and 3% sequentially in 2019 Q2, driven by lower shipments and average selling prices per ton.**  
   Consolidated net sales were \$5.90 billion in Q2 2019, down from \$6.46 billion in Q2 2018 and \$6.10 billion in Q1 2019. Average sales price per ton decreased 2% compared to Q2 2018 and 3% compared to Q1 2019. Shipments to outside customers totaled 6.72 million tons, down 7% year-over-year and 1% sequentially [8-K 2019-07-18; 10-Q 2019-08-07].

2. **Net earnings per diluted share fell 41% year-over-year and 23% sequentially, reflecting margin compression amid volume and price declines.**  
   Q2 2019 net earnings were \$386.5 million or \$1.26 per diluted share, versus \$683.2 million or \$2.13 per diluted share in Q2 2018 and \$501.8 million or \$1.63 per diluted share in Q1 2019. Net earnings as a percentage of net sales declined from 11% in Q2 2018 to 7% in Q2 2019. First half 2019 net earnings per diluted share of \$2.88 were down from \$3.23 in the first half of 2018 [8-K 2019-07-18; 10-Q 2019-08-07].

3. **Gross margins decreased significantly, with steel mills segment margins pressured by lower volumes and utilization despite lower scrap costs.**  
   Total gross margins were \$775.5 million (13%) in Q2 2019, down from \$1.17 billion (18%) in Q2 2018. Average scrap and scrap substitute costs per ton used in steel mills declined 12% year-over-year to \$330, outpacing the 2% decrease in average selling price per ton, which improved metal margin per ton. However, overall steel mill margins declined due to 10% lower shipments and a drop in operating rates from 95% to 84% [8-K 2019-07-18; 10-Q 2019-08-07].

4. **Pre-operating and start-up costs more than tripled year-over-year, increasing to \$20.5 million in Q2 2019, reflecting expansion projects.**  
   These costs, expensed as incurred, rose from \$5.8 million in Q2 2018 to \$20.5 million in Q2 2019, related primarily to new bar mills in Missouri and Florida and a galvanizing line and mill expansion at the Kentucky sheet mill. Such costs are expected to continue until facilities reach consistent utilization [8-K 2019-07-18; 10-Q 2019-08-07].

5. **Nucor maintained strong liquidity with \$1.48 billion in cash and short-term investments at June 29, 2019, and continued share repurchases.**  
   The company repurchased approximately 2.3 million shares in Q2 2019 at an average price of \$55.41, totaling about 3.5 million shares repurchased for the first half of 2019 at an average price of \$57.25. Approximately \$1.3 billion remained available under the share repurchase program [8-K 2019-07-18].

### Operations Insights

6. **Steel mill shipments declined 10% year-over-year and 3% sequentially, with significant volume drops in bars (-15%) and structural products (-11%).**  
   Total steel mill shipments were 5.8 million tons in Q2 2019 versus 6.44 million tons in Q2 2018. Shipments of bars decreased 15% year-over-year to 2.02 million tons, and structural shipments fell 11% to 556,000 tons. Shipments to outside customers from steel mills declined 8% year-over-year to 4.68 million tons [8-K 2019-07-18].

7. **Operating rates at steel mills dropped to 84% in Q2 2019 from 95% in Q2 2018, reflecting lower demand and customer inventory management.**  
   The sequential decrease from 87% in Q1 2019 and the year-over-year decline were attributed to service center destocking, increased domestic supply, and a declining scrap price environment, which led to cautious order rates and aggressive inventory management by customers [8-K 2019-07-18; 10-Q 2019-08-07].

8. **A planned outage at the Trinidad direct reduced iron (DRI) facility occurred from June 19 to July 13, 2019, affecting raw materials segment performance.**  
   The raw materials segment’s operating performance remained similar to Q1 2019 but is expected to decline in Q3 2019 due to margin compression in the DRI businesses. The DRI facilities provide operational flexibility to manage input costs, particularly scrap availability and pricing [8-K 2019-07-18; 10-Q 2019-08-07].

9. **Average scrap and scrap substitute costs declined 12% year-over-year and 6% sequentially to \$330 per ton, partially offsetting price declines.**  
   The first half of 2019 average scrap cost was \$341 per ton, down 4% from the first half of 2018. Lower scrap costs contributed to improved metal margin per ton in steel mills despite lower prices and volumes [8-K 2019-07-18; 10-Q 2019-08-07].

10. **Utilization rates decreased across segments: steel mills to 85% (from 93%), steel products to 68% (from 73%), and raw materials to 72% (from 76%) year-over-year in first half 2019.**  
    These declines align with reduced shipments and lower demand, with the steel mills segment showing the most pronounced drop. The steel products segment saw some improvement in profitability due to seasonal factors and better weather benefiting nonresidential construction markets [10-Q 2019-08-07].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

11. **Steel products segment profitability improved sequentially in Q2 2019 due to seasonal patterns and stronger nonresidential construction markets.**  
    Shipments of downstream steel products to outside customers increased 2% sequentially but decreased 4% year-over-year. Efficiency initiatives in rebar fabrication and metal buildings contributed to better segment performance despite challenging overall market conditions [8-K 2019-07-18; 10-Q 2019-08-07].

12. **Nucor announced a new 1.2 million ton annual capacity steel plate mill in Brandenburg, Kentucky, expected to be operational by 2022.**  
    This greenfield project will complement existing plate mills in North Carolina, Alabama, and Texas, allowing Nucor to produce approximately 97% of the products demanded in the domestic plate market, including specialty higher-margin products. The project will employ about 400 people [10-Q 2019-08-07].

### Wrap Up

Nucor’s 2019 Q2 results reflect a challenging steel market environment marked by lower shipments, softer average selling prices, and reduced operating rates, particularly in steel mills. Despite a beneficial decline in scrap input costs that improved metal margins per ton, overall earnings and gross margins contracted significantly year-over-year and sequentially due to volume declines and customer-driven inventory destocking. The steel products segment showed some resilience with improved profitability tied to seasonal and market factors. Operationally, a planned outage at the Trinidad DRI facility and increased pre-operating costs for expansion projects weighed on results. Nucor maintained strong liquidity and continued share repurchases, supporting financial flexibility.

Management’s outlook for Q3 2019 anticipates further pressure on steel mill segment earnings due to lower flat rolled and plate steel prices but expects steel products segment profitability to improve, supported by ongoing efficiency initiatives and stable nonresidential construction demand. The company also plans significant capital investments, including a new steel plate mill in Kentucky, signaling a strategic focus on expanding capacity for higher-value products despite near-term market headwinds.
2019.Q3:
### Financial Insights

1. **Nucor’s consolidated net earnings declined sharply in 2019Q3 amid lower steel prices and volumes.** The company reported net earnings of \$275.0 million (\$0.90 per diluted share) for the quarter ended September 28, 2019, down 59% from \$676.7 million (\$2.13 per diluted share) in 2018Q3 and down 29% from \$386.5 million (\$1.26 per diluted share) in 2019Q2 [8-K 2019-10-22; 10-Q 2019-11-06]. Net earnings as a percentage of net sales were 5% in 2019Q3 versus 10% in 2018Q3. For the first nine months of 2019, net earnings were \$1.16 billion (\$3.78 per diluted share), down 32% from \$1.71 billion (\$5.35 per diluted share) in the same period of 2018 [8-K 2019-10-22; 10-Q 2019-11-06]. Annualized return on average stockholders’ equity fell from 25% in 2018 YTD to 15% in 2019 YTD [10-Q 2019-11-06].

2. **Net sales decreased 19% year-over-year and 7% year-to-date, driven by lower steel prices and shipments.** Third quarter net sales were \$5.46 billion, down from \$6.74 billion in 2018Q3 and \$5.90 billion in 2019Q2. Average sales price per ton declined 13% versus 2018Q3 and 5% versus 2019Q2. Shipments to outside customers fell 7% year-over-year and 3% sequentially to 6.56 million tons [8-K 2019-10-22; 10-Q 2019-11-06]. Year-to-date net sales were \$17.46 billion, down 7% from \$18.77 billion in 2018 [10-Q 2019-11-06].

3. **Gross margins compressed sharply, especially in the steel mills segment, despite lower raw material costs.** Gross margin for the quarter was 10% (\$572.5 million) versus 19% in 2018Q3. The steel mills segment saw a 26% drop in net sales in 2019Q3 to \$3.24 billion from \$4.40 billion in 2018Q3, with segment earnings before tax falling from \$1.10 billion in 2018Q3 to \$310 million in 2019Q3. The primary driver was lower steel selling prices and volumes, despite a 20% decline in average scrap and scrap substitute cost per ton compared to 2018Q3 (\$299 versus \$374). Year-to-date, gross margins declined from 17% to 13%, primarily due to metal margin contraction in steel mills [8-K 2019-10-22; 10-Q 2019-11-06].

4. **Operating rates at steel mills declined to 83% in 2019Q3 from 92% in 2018Q3 and 84% in 2019Q2, reflecting softened market conditions.** The company cited destocking by customers and excess supply as key reasons for lower utilization. First nine months 2019 operating rates averaged 85%, down from 93% in 2018 [8-K 2019-10-22].

5. **Pre-operating and start-up costs for growth projects increased to \$28 million in 2019Q3 from \$11 million in 2018Q3, reflecting ongoing expansions.** These costs relate to new mills and expansions in Missouri, Florida, Arkansas, Kentucky, and Louisiana. These costs are expensed until facilities reach normal utilization [8-K 2019-10-22; 10-Q 2019-11-06].

6. **Nucor maintained a strong liquidity position with \$1.94 billion in cash, short-term investments, and an untapped \$1.5 billion revolving credit facility expiring in 2023.** No borrowings were outstanding on the credit facility as of September 28, 2019 [8-K 2019-10-22; 10-Q 2019-11-06].

7. **Capital expenditures for 2019 are expected to rise to approximately \$1.5 billion from \$997 million in 2018, driven by multiple major expansion projects.** These include hot band galvanizing lines, sheet mill expansions, greenfield micro mill expansions in Missouri and Florida, a merchant bar rolling facility in Illinois, and upgrades to the Louisiana DRI plant [10-Q 2019-11-06].

### Operations Insights

8. **Steel shipments to outside customers declined 7% year-to-date and 8% in 2019Q3 compared to 2018Q3, with the largest decreases in plate (-26%) and bars (-10%).** Shipments of plate fell from 633,000 tons in 2018Q3 to 470,000 tons in 2019Q3, while bar shipments declined from 2.27 million tons to 2.03 million tons. Some downstream steel product shipments (joist, deck, fabricated concrete reinforcing steel, piling, tubular products) showed small increases or were stable [8-K 2019-10-22].

9. **The raw materials segment’s performance declined due to margin compression and a planned outage at the Louisiana direct reduced iron (DRI) plant lasting until mid-November 2019.** Raw materials net sales fell 19% in 2019Q3 and 15% year-to-date, primarily due to lower selling prices at the brokerage operations and lower volumes. The raw materials segment reported a loss of \$10.6 million in 2019Q3 compared to a loss of \$29.1 million in 2018Q3, indicating some improvement but continued pressure [8-K 2019-10-22; 10-Q 2019-11-06].

10. **Efficiency initiatives in steel products—particularly in rebar fabrication and metal buildings—improved profitability despite overall market softness.** The steel products segment’s earnings before tax increased to \$170.2 million in 2019Q3 from \$138.7 million in 2018Q3, even as net sales declined slightly (down 2% in the quarter) [8-K 2019-10-22].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

11. **Market conditions softened for plate and sheet steel in 2019Q3, leading to customer destocking and excess inventory in the supply chain, which pressured prices and volumes.** Despite this, nonresidential construction markets remained strong, supporting steel products segment profitability [8-K 2019-10-22].

12. **Nucor’s product portfolio expansion includes a new state-of-the-art plate mill under construction in Brandenburg, Kentucky, expected to be fully operational in 2022 with 1.2 million tons annual capacity.** This facility will complement existing plate mills and enable production of approximately 97% of domestic plate products, including higher-margin specialty products [10-Q 2019-11-06].

### Corporate and Risk Insights

13. **Nucor’s exposure to market risk includes price fluctuations in scrap, iron ore, and natural gas, which are partly hedged through derivative instruments.** At September 28, 2019, unrealized net-of-tax losses on derivatives were \$12.8 million. The company also hedges natural gas price risk for the Louisiana DRI plant and steel mills [10-Q 2019-11-06].

14. **No impairment charges were recorded in 2019Q3, contrasting with a \$110 million impairment related to natural gas well assets in 2018Q3.** Equity investments in unconsolidated affiliates declined in earnings due to margin compression and volume decreases, notably at NuMit [10-Q 2019-11-06].

15. **The company declared its 186th consecutive quarterly dividend of \$0.40 per share payable November 8, 2019, reflecting a stable capital return policy despite earnings pressures.** Nucor intends to return at least 40% of net earnings to shareholders while maintaining investment-grade credit metrics [8-K 2019-10-22; 10-Q 2019-11-06].

16. **Outlook for 2019Q4 anticipates earnings declines across all segments due to lower steel prices, normal seasonality in steel products, and the continuation of the Louisiana DRI plant outage.** Management believes steel prices have bottomed at the end of 2019Q3 but expects further margin pressures [8-K 2019-10-22].

### Wrap Up

Nucor’s 2019 third quarter results reflect a marked downturn driven by weaker steel market pricing and softened demand, especially in plate and sheet products, which led to lower shipments, reduced operating rates, and compressed margins in the steel mills segment. While raw material costs declined significantly, this was insufficient to offset the impact of falling steel prices and volumes. The steel products segment showed resilience with improved profitability supported by efficiency gains and stable nonresidential construction demand. The company is investing heavily in growth projects, incurring increased start-up costs, and maintaining a strong liquidity position with nearly \$2 billion in cash and credit availability. Nucor continues its dividend program and plans capital expenditures near \$1.5 billion for 2019, emphasizing expansions that will broaden its product portfolio, including a new plate mill expected in 2022.

Management’s outlook for the fourth quarter of 2019 signals further earnings declines, primarily due to lower steel prices and a planned outage at the Louisiana DRI plant extending into mid-November, alongside typical seasonal softness in steel products. The company’s risk exposure to raw material and energy price fluctuations is managed through hedging programs, but margin pressures persist. No major operational disruptions or impairments were reported in 2019Q3, and the company’s conservative financial practices provide flexibility amid challenging market conditions.
2019.Q4:
### Financial Insights

1. **Nucor’s 2019Q4 earnings declined sharply due to lower steel prices and non-cash impairments, with net earnings of \$107.8 million (\$0.35 per diluted share) compared to \$275.0 million (\$0.90 per diluted share) in 2019Q3 and \$646.8 million (\$2.07 per diluted share) in 2018Q4.**  
   The fourth quarter included \$66.9 million in non-cash impairment charges (\$0.17 per diluted share), split across segments: \$35.0 million related to natural gas well assets in raw materials, \$20.0 million on long-lived assets in steel mills, and \$11.9 million on intangible assets in steel products. Excluding these impairments, earnings were still down due to a 5% decrease in average steel sales price per ton from Q3 and volume declines. For full-year 2019, net earnings were \$1.27 billion (\$4.14 per diluted share), down 46% from \$2.36 billion (\$7.42 per diluted share) in 2018, reflecting a 10% sales decrease to \$22.59 billion and a 5% shipment decline to 26.53 million tons [8-K 2020-01-28; 10-K 2020-02-28].

2. **Steel sales prices and volumes declined in 2019Q4 amid ongoing inventory destocking, with average sales price per ton down 5% from Q3 and shipments down 1%.**  
   Total shipments to outside customers in Q4 were 6.49 million tons, a 1% decrease versus Q3 and 3% lower than Q4 2018. Average sales price per ton fell 16% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. Despite stable steel mill shipments internally, shipments to external customers declined. Overall net sales dropped 6% sequentially and 18% year-over-year to \$5.13 billion in Q4 [8-K 2020-01-28].

3. **Gross margins and metal margins compressed due to lower steel prices despite a 13% year-over-year decline in scrap and scrap substitute costs, which averaged \$275 per gross ton in Q4 2019 (down 8% sequentially and 23% year-over-year).**  
   Scrap costs per gross ton used averaged \$314 for full-year 2019, down 13% from \$361 in 2018. However, metal margin—the difference between steel selling price and scrap cost—declined due to lower selling prices and reduced volumes. This margin compression was a key driver of profit declines in the steel mills segment [8-K 2020-01-28; 10-K 2020-02-28].

4. **Pre-operating and start-up costs for growth projects increased to \$35 million in Q4 2019 (\$0.09 per diluted share), up from \$28 million (\$0.07 per diluted share) in Q3 2019, reflecting ongoing investments in new facilities and expansions.**  
   For full-year 2019, these costs totaled approximately \$103 million (\$0.26 per diluted share), nearly tripling from \$36 million (\$0.09 per diluted share) in 2018. Projects contributing include expansions at bar mills in Missouri and Florida, cold mill expansion in Arkansas, and sheet mill expansions in Kentucky and Arkansas [8-K 2020-01-28; 10-Q 2019-11-06].

5. **Nucor maintained strong liquidity with \$1.83 billion in cash and short-term investments at December 31, 2019, and an untapped \$1.5 billion revolving credit facility available through April 2023.**  
   During Q4, the company repurchased 1.9 million shares at an average price of \$54.61, totaling approximately \$104 million. For the full year 2019, share repurchases were about 5.3 million shares at an average price of \$56.33, with \$1.2 billion remaining authorized under the repurchase program [8-K 2020-01-28; 8-K 2019-10-22].

### Operations Insights

6. **Steel mill operating rates remained stable at 83% in Q4 2019 but down from 88% in Q4 2018 and 85% for full-year 2019, reflecting weaker demand and ongoing destocking.**  
   The company’s total steel mill shipments declined 2% sequentially and 6% year-over-year to 5.78 million tons in Q4 2019. Shipments by product showed mixed trends: sheet shipments increased 3% year-over-year but plate shipments fell 18%. Internal steel mill shipments to downstream steel products remained steady at 21% of total steel mill shipments [8-K 2020-01-28].

7. **A planned 70-day outage at Nucor’s Louisiana direct reduced iron (DRI) plant, from early September to mid-November 2019, negatively impacted raw materials segment profitability in Q4.**  
   The raw materials segment recorded a loss of \$92.6 million in Q4 2019 compared to a profit of \$55.8 million in Q4 2018, largely due to the outage and a \$35 million impairment on natural gas well assets. Margin compression also affected other raw materials businesses, including scrap brokerage and processing [8-K 2020-01-28; 10-K 2020-02-28].

8. **Nucor’s steel products segment showed slight sequential earnings decline in Q4 2019 due to normal year-end seasonality, despite a 3% increase in shipments of deck and joist products year-over-year.**  
   Shipments to outside customers for steel products increased 8% from Q3 2019 but were mixed by product line: tubular products shipments rose 19% year-over-year, piling products increased 39%, while cold finished steel shipments dropped 18%. Earnings before taxes in steel products were \$147.4 million in Q4, up from \$86.8 million in Q4 2018, indicating some resilience despite seasonal pressure [8-K 2020-01-28].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

9. **Inventory destocking in 2019, particularly in plate and sheet markets, pressured prices and volumes but appeared to conclude in Q4 2019 as customers resumed normal buying patterns and Nucor announced price increases.**  
   Management indicated that the destocking cycle ended in Q4, contributing to better-than-expected steel mill segment earnings in December 2019. Price increases announced in Q4 for sheet, bar, plate, and structural products are expected to benefit Q1 2020 results [8-K 2020-01-28; 10-K 2020-02-28].

10. **Nucor expanded its product portfolio with acquisitions and capital projects aimed at higher value-added products, including the December 2019 acquisition of TrueCore, LLC, an insulated metal panel manufacturer serving the cold storage market.**  
    Additionally, the company announced a coil paint line expansion at its Arkansas sheet mill, expected online in 2022, and continues ramping up a new hot band galvanizing and pickling line in Kentucky, enhancing automotive market capabilities [8-K 2020-01-28; 10-K 2020-02-28].

### Corporate and Risk Insights

11. **Nucor disclosed ongoing exposure to market risks from fluctuations in steel prices, raw material costs (including scrap and iron ore), energy prices, and trade policies, with the steel mills and steel products segments being the largest risk areas.**  
    The company’s vertical integration, including in-house DRI production and scrap brokerage, provides some raw material cost control but does not eliminate market risk. The Louisiana DRI outage and impairment charges highlight operational risks in raw materials. Trade policies, particularly Section 232 tariffs, reduced imports by 18% in 2019, supporting domestic pricing [10-K 2020-02-28; 10-Q 2019-11-06; 8-K 2020-01-28].

### Wrap Up

Nucor’s fourth quarter of 2019 reflected a continuation of the challenging steel market environment that pressured prices, volumes, and margins throughout the year. The quarter’s net earnings declined sharply to \$107.8 million (\$0.35 per diluted share), weighed down by lower steel prices, ongoing inventory destocking earlier in the year, a significant Louisiana DRI plant outage, and non-cash impairment charges totaling \$66.9 million. Despite stable steel mill operating rates and increased shipments in some steel product lines, the overall volume and pricing environment remained subdued compared to 2018.

The company’s cost structure benefited from lower scrap prices, which fell 23% year-over-year in Q4, but this was insufficient to offset the decline in steel selling prices and volumes. Investments in growth projects increased pre-operating costs, reflecting Nucor’s strategy to expand its product offerings, including higher value-added steel and insulated panels. Liquidity remained strong with nearly \$1.83 billion in cash and short-term investments and a \$1.5 billion credit facility.

Management indicated that inventory destocking concluded in Q4 2019, with price increases announced late in the quarter expected to support earnings improvement in Q1 2020. The Louisiana DRI outage and impairment charges are notable operational risks, alongside broader exposure to commodity price volatility, energy costs, and trade policy uncertainties.

**Guidance for Q1 2020** anticipates increased steel mills segment earnings (excluding the Q4 impairment charges) driven by price increases and higher volumes, a slight seasonal earnings decline in steel products, and a raw materials segment recovery due to improved pricing and absence of outages or impairments [8-K 2020-01-28; 10-K 2020-02-28]. No other material risks or events specifically affecting near-term operations were disclosed.
2019.FY:
### Financial Insights

1. **Nucor's 2019 net earnings declined by 46% to \$1.27 billion from \$2.36 billion in 2018, reflecting lower sales and margin compression across segments.**  
   For the full year 2019, Nucor reported consolidated net earnings of \$1.27 billion, or \$4.14 per diluted share, down from \$2.36 billion, or \$7.42 per diluted share, in 2018. Net earnings as a percentage of net sales dropped to 5.6% in 2019 from 9.4% in 2018. Return on average stockholders’ equity declined to 12.6% from 25.5% the prior year [10-K filed 2020-02-28].  
   Consolidated net sales decreased 10% to \$22.59 billion in 2019 from \$25.07 billion in 2018, driven by a 5% decline in total tons shipped to outside customers (26.53 million tons vs. 27.90 million tons) and a 5% decrease in average sales price per ton [8-K filed 2020-01-28].  
   Cost of products sold fell less proportionally, to \$19.91 billion from \$20.77 billion, contributing to margin pressure [8-K filed 2020-01-28].

2. **Steel mills segment earnings halved in 2019 due to a 14% sales decline and lower metal margins, while steel products segment earnings improved slightly on a 3% sales increase.**  
   Steel mills net sales to external customers dropped from \$16.25 billion in 2018 to \$13.93 billion in 2019 (-14%), with segment earnings before income taxes decreasing from \$3.50 billion in 2018 to \$1.79 billion in 2019 [10-K filed 2020-02-28; 8-K filed 2020-01-28]. This was attributed to lower average selling prices and metal margins, especially for sheet, bar, and structural products, combined with reduced shipments and operating rates (84% in 2019 vs. 91% in 2018) [10-K filed 2020-02-28; 8-K filed 2019-10-22].  
   Conversely, the steel products segment saw net sales grow modestly by 3% to \$6.99 billion in 2019 from \$6.80 billion in 2018, with earnings before income taxes increasing from \$467 million to \$511 million, supported by strong performance in metal buildings, piling, joist, deck, and rebar fabrication divisions [10-K filed 2020-02-28; 8-K filed 2019-10-22].

3. **Raw materials segment profitability deteriorated sharply in 2019, with an 18% sales decline and margin compression exacerbated by a 70-day outage at the Louisiana DRI plant.**  
   Raw materials segment net sales fell from \$2.03 billion in 2018 to \$1.66 billion in 2019 (-18%), and the segment swung from \$236 million in earnings before income taxes in 2018 to a loss of \$28 million in 2019 [10-K filed 2020-02-28; 8-K filed 2020-01-28].  
   This was driven by margin compression due to lower average selling prices for raw materials, increased iron ore costs, and a planned 70-day outage at the Louisiana DRI facility from early September to mid-November 2019 [10-K filed 2020-02-28; 10-Q filed 2019-11-06].  
   Additionally, a non-cash impairment charge of \$35 million related to natural gas well assets in the raw materials segment was recorded in Q4 2019 [8-K filed 2020-01-28].

4. **Average scrap and scrap substitute costs used in steel production declined 13% in 2019 to \$314 per gross ton, partially relieving input cost pressure.**  
   The average scrap and scrap substitute cost per gross ton used decreased from \$361 in 2018 to \$314 in 2019. Quarterly costs showed a downward trend, with Q4 2019 cost at \$275 per gross ton, down 23% from \$359 in Q4 2018 [8-K filed 2020-01-28; 8-K filed 2019-04-23].  
   Nucor uses approximately 1.1 tons of scrap and substitutes to produce one ton of steel, making scrap costs a significant input expense [10-K filed 2020-02-28].

5. **Pre-operating and start-up costs related to growth projects increased sharply to approximately \$103 million in 2019, reflecting ongoing capital expansions.**  
   Pre-operating and start-up costs rose from \$36 million in 2018 to \$103 million in 2019, or \$0.26 per diluted share, reflecting costs associated with multiple growth projects [8-K filed 2020-01-28].  
   These costs increased sequentially each quarter, reaching \$35 million in Q4 2019 [8-K filed 2020-01-28].

6. **Nucor maintained a strong liquidity position with \$1.83 billion in cash and short-term investments and an undrawn \$1.5 billion revolving credit facility as of year-end 2019.**  
   Cash and cash equivalents rose from \$1.40 billion at year-end 2018 to \$1.53 billion at year-end 2019, with short-term investments increasing from zero to \$300 million [8-K filed 2020-01-28].  
   The company’s funded debt to total capital ratio was stable at approximately 29%, with no material debt maturities until 2022 [10-K filed 2020-02-28].

7. **Capital expenditures surged to approximately \$1.8 billion in 2019 from \$997 million in 2018, driven by multiple major expansion and upgrade projects.**  
   Key projects underway included:  
   - Hot band galvanizing and sheet mill expansion at Nucor Steel Gallatin (\$650 million plus \$176 million)  
   - Specialty cold mill complex at Nucor Steel Arkansas (\$230 million)  
   - Two micro mill greenfield expansions in Sedalia, Missouri and Frostproof, Florida (\$250 million and \$240 million respectively)  
   - Merchant bar rolling facility expansion at Nucor Steel Kankakee (\$180 million)  
   - New steel plate mill in Brandenburg, Kentucky, announced in March 2019, with estimated \$1.35 billion capex, expected operational in 2022 [10-Q filed 2019-05-08; 10-K filed 2020-02-28; 8-K filed 2019-04-23].

### Operations Insights

8. **Steel mill operating rates decreased to 84% in 2019 from 91% in 2018, reflecting weaker demand and customer inventory destocking.**  
   Quarterly operating rates declined from 88% in Q4 2018 to 83% in Q3 and Q4 2019 [8-K filed 2019-10-22; 8-K filed 2020-01-28].  
   Destocking by service center customers and excess supply in sheet and plate products pressured shipments and utilization, especially in the second half of 2019 [8-K filed 2019-10-22].  
   Total steel mill shipments to outside customers declined 7% in the first nine months of 2019 compared to 2018, with specific declines in bars (-12%), plate (-10%), and structural products (-8%) [8-K filed 2019-10-22].

9. **Downstream steel products shipments showed mixed trends, with some growth in piling (+13%) and joist (+2%) but declines in cold finished (-12%) and tubular products (-11%) year-over-year for 2019.**  
   Total downstream steel products shipments to outside customers decreased 5% in 2019 compared to 2018 [8-K filed 2020-01-28].  
   Efficiency initiatives improved performance in rebar fabrication and metal buildings businesses, partially offsetting weaker sheet mill results [8-K filed 2019-10-22].

10. **The Louisiana DRI plant experienced a planned 70-day outage in Q3-Q4 2019, significantly impacting raw materials segment margins and steel mill inputs.**  
    The outage began in early September and ended mid-November 2019, contributing to margin compression in raw materials and lower raw materials segment profitability in Q4 2019 [10-K filed 2020-02-28; 10-Q filed 2019-11-06].  
    This outage was a factor in a sharp decline in raw materials segment earnings to a loss in 2019 [8-K filed 2020-01-28].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

11. **Average sales price per ton declined 5% in 2019, reflecting a more challenging steel pricing environment following record 2018 prices.**  
    Average sales price per ton fell 5% year-over-year, contributing to a 10% decrease in total net sales [8-K filed 2020-01-28].  
    Quarterly average prices declined sequentially in 2019, with Q4 2019 prices down 16% compared to Q4 2018, and down 5% from Q3 2019 [8-K filed 2020-01-28].  
    Management attributed price declines to aggressive customer inventory destocking and softened market conditions for sheet and plate products [8-K filed 2019-10-22].

12. **Nucor’s product mix shift towards value-added and specialty steel products continued, supported by ongoing capital investments in galvanizing lines, cold mills, and a new plate mill.**  
    The new plate mill in Brandenburg, Kentucky, announced in March 2019, will have 1.2 million tons annual capacity and is expected to produce 97% of the domestic plate market product range, including specialty higher-margin products [10-Q filed 2019-11-06; 8-K filed 2019-04-23].  
    Investments in hot band galvanizing lines at Arkansas and Gallatin steel mills and the specialty cold mill complex at Arkansas aim to expand advanced high-strength and motor lamination steel production [10-K filed 2019-02-28].  
    The acquisition of TrueCore, LLC in December 2019 added insulated metal panel manufacturing capabilities to serve cold storage and industrial markets [8-K filed 2020-01-28].

### Corporate and Risk Insights

13. **Nucor identified risks from global steel industry overcapacity and import competition, but Section 232 tariffs helped reduce unfairly traded imports to the U.S. in 2019.**  
    Finished steel imports into the U.S. decreased approximately 18% in 2019, reaching the lowest market share since 2010 at 19% of the U.S. market [10-K filed 2020-02-28].  
    The company cited risks including competitive pressure on sales and pricing, U.S. and foreign trade policies, sensitivity to raw material prices, and energy cost and availability [8-K filed 2019-01-29; 8-K filed 2020-01-28].

### Wrap Up

In 2019, Nucor faced a challenging steel market environment marked by declining steel prices, reduced shipments, and margin compression, leading to a near-halving of net earnings compared to 2018. The steel mills segment experienced a notable sales and margin contraction, while the steel products segment showed modest growth supported by efficiency gains. The raw materials segment suffered from margin pressure exacerbated by a significant outage at the Louisiana DRI plant and lower raw material prices. Operating rates and shipments declined across the board, reflecting customer destocking and softer demand, particularly in sheet and plate steel.

Nucor continued to invest heavily in capital projects aimed at expanding its value-added product offerings and improving operational capabilities, including a new plate mill planned for 2022 and multiple galvanizing and cold mill expansions. The company maintained a strong liquidity position and manageable leverage, enabling it to pursue these strategic growth initiatives despite market headwinds. Risks remain from import competition and raw material cost volatility, though trade measures contributed to reducing unfairly traded imports in 2019.

**Forward-Looking Guidance:** For Q1 2020, Nucor expects earnings improvement compared to Q4 2019 (excluding impairment charges) driven by announced price increases and higher volumes in the steel mills segment, a more stable pricing environment following 2019 destocking, and improved raw materials segment performance due to better pricing and no planned outages at the Louisiana DRI plant. The steel products segment is expected to see a seasonal earnings decline in Q1 2020 [8-K filed 2020-01-28; 10-K filed 2020-02-28].

2020.Q1:
### Financial Insights

1. **Nucor’s net earnings collapsed to \$20.3 million in 2020Q1, down from \$501.8 million in 2019Q1, driven largely by a \$287.8 million impairment loss on its Italian joint venture Duferdofin Nucor.**  
   Consolidated net earnings fell to \$20.3 million, or \$0.07 per diluted share, in 2020Q1 from \$501.8 million, or \$1.63 per diluted share, in 2019Q1. This steep decline included a \$287.8 million (\$0.92 per diluted share) loss on assets related to the equity method investment in Duferdofin Nucor. The impairment charge of \$250 million was non-cash and reflected a triggering event due to adverse commercial outlook worsened by the COVID-19 pandemic. Additionally, a €35 million (\$37.8 million) note receivable from the joint venture was fully reserved, recorded in corporate/eliminations. Excluding these charges, earnings were slightly below prior guidance but still markedly lower than the prior year. The effective tax rate rose to 62.8% from 23.0%, primarily due to the impairment which did not reduce tax provision [8-K 2020-04-28; 10-Q 2020-05-13].

2. **Net sales declined 8% year-over-year to \$5.62 billion despite tonnage shipped increasing 6%, reflecting a 13% drop in average sales price per ton.**  
   Total shipments to outside customers rose 6% to 7.187 million tons, but average sales price per ton fell 13% from \$901 in 2019Q1 to \$783 in 2020Q1. Net sales decreased from \$6.10 billion to \$5.62 billion. The steel mills segment’s net sales dropped 11% to \$3.52 billion, while the steel products segment grew 4% to \$1.73 billion. The raw materials segment’s sales decreased 23% to \$378 million, mainly due to lower prices and volumes in scrap brokerage and processing. Intercompany sales adjustments were significant but stable [8-K 2020-04-28; 10-Q 2020-05-13].

3. **Gross margins contracted to 11% in 2020Q1 from 15% in 2019Q1, reflecting lower metal margins and the Duferdofin impairment.**  
   Gross margin dollars fell to \$629.3 million from \$895.9 million. The steel mills segment earnings before taxes declined sharply from \$689.4 million to \$156.5 million, driven by lower selling prices, metal margins, and the \$250 million impairment. Conversely, the steel products segment improved earnings before taxes from \$77.4 million to \$162.6 million, supported by increased gross margins despite lower average prices. The raw materials segment swung from a \$53.2 million profit to a \$7.9 million loss, losing the prior year’s \$33.7 million gain on sale of an equity interest and experiencing weaker DRI and scrap brokerage performance. Corporate/eliminations losses widened, mainly due to the \$37.8 million note receivable write-off [10-Q 2020-05-13].

4. **Cash flow from operations declined to \$201.2 million from \$650.7 million in 2019Q1, pressured by working capital build and the impairment charge.**  
   The \$476.4 million net earnings drop, including \$287.8 million non-cash losses, contributed to weaker cash generation. Working capital changes used \$366.7 million of cash, driven by a \$124 million increase in accounts receivable (reflecting 11% higher shipments) and a \$42 million rise in inventories, partly from a 4% increase in scrap cost in inventory. Salaries and wages accruals decreased less than prior year, partially offsetting cash use. Capital expenditures were estimated below \$1.5 billion for 2020, with major projects including expansions and greenfield mills in Arkansas, Gallatin, Florida, and Kentucky [10-Q 2020-05-13].

5. **Liquidity remained strong with \$1.39 billion in cash and short-term investments and an undrawn \$1.5 billion revolving credit facility; no significant debt maturities until September 2022.**  
   The company maintained compliance with credit covenants and credit ratings of Baa1/A- with stable outlooks. Nucor repurchased 0.8 million shares at an average price of \$47.88 per share in 2020Q1, with \$1.16 billion remaining authorized for repurchase. The board declared a cash dividend of \$0.4025 per share payable May 11, 2020, continuing a 47-year streak of dividend increases [8-K 2020-04-28; 10-Q 2020-05-13].

### Operations Insights

6. **Steel mills utilization increased to 89% in 2020Q1 from 83% in 2019Q4 and 87% in 2019Q1, supporting higher shipments despite COVID-19 disruptions late in the quarter.**  
   Total steel mill shipments rose 8% year-over-year to 6.498 million tons, with outside shipments up 9%. Shipments grew across sheet (+9%), bars (+12%), structural (+21%), and plate (+1%) products. Internal shipments represented 20% of steel mill shipments, stable with prior periods. Steel products shipments to outside customers increased 13%, led by joist (+19%), deck (+18%), fabricated concrete reinforcing steel (+20%), and piling (+30%). Cold finished steel shipments declined 12%. Production at the Louisiana DRI facility was halted April 2 due to COVID-19 but resumed April 25 with enhanced safety protocols. The Trinidad DRI facility stopped production March 30 following government orders [8-K 2020-04-28; 10-Q 2020-05-13].

7. **Raw material costs showed mixed trends: average scrap cost per ton used was \$293 in 2020Q1, down 17% year-over-year but up 7% sequentially.**  
   This indicates some pricing volatility amid the pandemic. The raw materials segment faced volume and price declines in scrap brokerage and processing. Nucor’s DRI facilities provide operational flexibility to manage input costs when scrap prices rise. The company uses derivative instruments to hedge natural gas, scrap, aluminum, and copper price risks, with unrealized net-of-tax losses of \$14.2 million on derivatives at quarter-end. Commodity price risk sensitivity analysis showed potential pre-tax earnings impacts of \$7.4 million (10% natural gas price change) to \$18.5 million (25%) [8-K 2020-04-28; 10-Q 2020-05-13].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

8. **Average sales price per ton declined 13% year-over-year and 1% sequentially, despite tonnage growth, reflecting weak market pricing and COVID-19 impact on demand.**  
   The company shipped 7.187 million tons to outside customers, up 11% from 2019Q4 and 6% from 2019Q1, but average selling price fell from \$901 to \$783 per ton year-over-year. This price decline pressured steel mills segment revenue and gross margins. Downstream steel products saw shipment increases but mixed pricing impacts, with cold finished steel shipments down 12%. The largest end market, nonresidential construction, showed resilience with project delays rather than cancellations, while automotive and energy markets experienced sharp declines. Competitors’ capacity idling also influenced market conditions [8-K 2020-04-28; 10-Q 2020-05-13].

### Corporate and Risk Insights

9. **COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted operations and outlook, causing a triggering event for the Duferdofin Nucor impairment and prompting temporary production halts at DRI facilities.**  
   The pandemic’s effects varied by product group, with automotive and energy hardest hit and nonresidential construction more resilient. Nucor expects a likely loss in 2020Q2 due to uncertain market conditions but anticipates a bottoming in 2020Q2 and a return to profitability in the second half of 2020. The company highlighted supply-side responses including competitor capacity idling. Safety measures and production adjustments were implemented at key facilities to protect employees [8-K 2020-04-28; 10-Q 2020-05-13].

10. **Foreign currency translation losses increased sharply to \$64.5 million in 2020Q1 from \$6.6 million in 2019Q1, reflecting exposure in Europe and Canada.**  
    Nucor’s foreign operations in these regions contributed to a comprehensive loss attributable to stockholders of \$44.3 million, compared to comprehensive income of \$495.3 million in 2019Q1. Currency risk is partially mitigated by derivative contracts, though open foreign currency derivatives were insignificant at quarter-end [10-Q 2020-05-13].

### Wrap Up

Nucor’s 2020Q1 results reveal a steep earnings decline driven primarily by a \$287.8 million impairment loss on its Italian joint venture, Duferdofin Nucor, exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic’s disruption of market demand and operations. Despite a 6% rise in tonnage shipped, average selling prices fell 13% year-over-year, compressing revenues and gross margins, especially in the steel mills and raw materials segments. Operationally, steel mills improved utilization and shipments, while raw material costs showed volatility amid pandemic uncertainty. Liquidity remained strong, supported by \$1.39 billion in cash and an undrawn credit facility, with ongoing capital investment projects prioritized but flexible. The pandemic’s impact on end markets was uneven, with automotive and energy suffering sharp declines, while nonresidential construction showed resilience. Currency translation losses and market uncertainty contributed to a comprehensive loss.

**Guidance Overview:** Nucor expects second quarter 2020 losses due to continued pandemic-driven economic uncertainty but anticipates market conditions to bottom in 2Q20 and a return to profitability in the second half of 2020. The company is managing capital expenditures below \$1.5 billion for 2020, focusing on high-impact projects while maintaining dividend payments and share repurchases within authorized programs. No significant debt maturities are due before September 2022.

### Financial Insights

8. **Nucor maintained its 189th consecutive quarterly dividend at \$0.4025 per share payable August 11, 2020.** The Board declared this dividend on June 4, 2020, reflecting a commitment to shareholder returns despite earnings volatility [8-K 2020-07-23, 10-Q 2020-08-12].

### Operations Insights

9. **Steel mill shipments declined sharply across product categories in 2020Q2, with sheet down 23% year-over-year and bars down 14%.** Total steel mill shipments were 4.77 million tons in 2020Q2, down 18% from 5.80 million tons in 2019Q2. ### Commercial Strategy Insights

13. **Average steel selling prices per ton declined 10% year-over-year but increased 1% sequentially in 2Q20, reflecting weak demand and pricing pressure from COVID-19.** Despite a slight price improvement from 1Q20, average selling prices remained significantly below 2019 levels. 14. **Steel mill shipments to internal customers represented 21% of total steel mill shipments in 2Q20, consistent with prior periods.** This reflects the integrated nature of Nucor’s operations, where steel produced in mills is partially consumed by downstream steel product segments [8-K 2020-07-23].

15. **Margins in the steel products segment improved year-over-year, driven by rebar fabrication and tubular products benefiting from resilient nonresidential construction demand, partially offset by weaker cold finished steel margins.** Gross margins in steel products increased despite overall market weakness, reflecting product mix and end-market differences [10-Q 2020-08-12].

### Corporate and Risk Insights

16. **Nucor recorded a \$255 million non-cash impairment charge on its equity method investment in Duferdofin Nucor and a \$37.8 million reserve on a note receivable from the joint venture, reflecting strategic and market challenges exacerbated by COVID-19.** These charges were included in the steel mills segment and corporate/eliminations line, significantly impacting first quarter 2020 results [10-Q 2020-08-12].

17. **The effective income tax rate increased to 26.5% in 2Q20 from 22.9% in 2Q19, primarily due to a \$5.3 million unfavorable non-cash, out-of-period adjustment to deferred tax balances.** Tax years 2015 through 2018 remain open to IRS examination, and Canadian tax returns for 2015 are under review, indicating ongoing tax audit risk [10-Q 2020-08-12].

18. **Nucor’s market risk exposure includes raw material price fluctuations, particularly scrap steel and natural gas, which it manages through procurement strategies and derivative hedging.** At July 4, 2020, unrealized net-of-tax losses on derivative instruments totaled \$10.9 million. The company expects scrap prices to remain stable entering 3Q20 [10-Q 2020-08-12].

19. **Liquidity is supported by strong cash balances, undrawn \$1.5 billion revolving credit facility, and investment-grade credit ratings (A- S&P, Baa1 Moody’s), although ratings are subject to change.** The company’s successful issuance of low coupon debt in 2Q20 enhances its financial flexibility amid the pandemic [10-Q 2020-08-12].

### Wrap Up

Nucor’s 2020 second quarter results reflect the material operational and financial impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, with sharply lower shipments and revenues leading to compressed margins and earnings well below 2019 levels. The company’s steel mills operated at significantly reduced capacity, and steel shipments declined across all major product lines. Lower scrap costs partially offset price and volume declines but were insufficient to preserve prior margin levels. The steel products segment showed some margin resilience driven by nonresidential construction markets.

Financially, Nucor strengthened liquidity through \$1 billion in low-cost debt issuances and maintained its long-standing dividend, signaling confidence in cash flow sufficiency despite earnings volatility. Capital spending was cautiously reaccelerated on key growth projects with attractive economic returns, balancing investment with liquidity preservation. The company also recognized substantial non-cash impairment charges related to its Italian joint venture, reflecting pandemic-related disruptions to international operations.

Management’s outlook for raw material prices entering 3Q20 is stable, but ongoing COVID-19 uncertainties and market conditions continue to pose risks. Nucor’s integrated business model, diversified product mix, and financial resources provide operational flexibility, but the pandemic’s impact on demand and pricing remains the dominant factor shaping near-term performance.

   Earnings before taxes in 2020Q3 were \$205.2 million for steel mills (down from \$309.9 million in 2019Q3 but up from 2020Q2), \$187.0 million for steel products (up from \$170.2 million in 2019Q3 and higher than 2020Q2), and \$6.2 million for raw materials (versus a \$10.6 million loss in 2019Q3) [8-K 2020-10-22]. The raw materials segment’s earnings improved due to better pricing and margins at direct reduced iron (DRI) facilities [8-K 2020-10-22; 10-Q 2020-11-12].

5. **Operating rates increased sequentially but remained below prior-year levels, reflecting ongoing demand challenges**  
   Steel mill operating rates rose to 83% in 2020Q3 from 68% in 2020Q2 but were flat compared to 83% in 2019Q3. For the first nine months of 2020, average utilization was 80%, down from 85% in 2019 [8-K 2020-10-22; 10-Q 2020-11-12]. Steel products and raw materials segments showed utilization at approximately 71% and 65%, respectively, for the first nine months of 2020, compared with 71% and 70% in the prior year [10-Q 2020-11-12].

6. **Capital expenditures were moderated amid the pandemic but selectively reaccelerated on key projects**  
   Nucor revised its 2020 capital expenditure estimate from an original \$2.0 billion to less than \$1.5 billion early in the year, then raised it to \$1.7 billion as of 2020Q3 [10-Q 2020-11-12]. The company paused some projects but reaccelerated investments in the Brandenburg, Kentucky plate mill and the Gallatin, Kentucky sheet mill expansion after review [10-Q 2020-11-12].

7. **Liquidity remained strong with \$3.41 billion in cash and equivalents plus an undrawn \$1.5 billion revolving credit facility**  
   At 2020Q3 end, cash and cash equivalents totaled \$2.87 billion, with additional short-term investments and restricted cash bringing total liquidity to \$3.41 billion. The revolving credit facility remained fully available and extends to April 2023 [8-K 2020-10-22; 10-Q 2020-11-12]. Nucor’s credit ratings remained stable at Baa1/A- [8-K 2020-10-22].

8. **Debt increased due to new bond issuances to fund capital projects, including \$500 million notes due 2025, \$500 million notes due 2030, and \$162.6 million in 40-year Green Bonds**  
   Nucor issued \$1 billion in low-coupon notes and became an obligor on \$162.6 million in Green Bonds in 2020 to partially finance the Kentucky plate mill [10-Q 2020-11-12]. Long-term debt rose from \$4.29 billion at end-2019 to \$5.45 billion at 2020Q3 [10-Q 2020-11-12].

### Operations Insights

9. **Steel mill shipments increased 18% sequentially but declined 3% year-over-year; product mix shifts showed strength in bars and structural products**  
   Total steel mill shipments were 5.63 million tons in 2020Q3, up 18% from 2020Q2 but down 3% from 2019Q3 [8-K 2020-10-22]. Shipments of bars grew 4% year-over-year, structural products rose 4%, while sheet shipments declined 7% and plate shipments fell 10% year-over-year [8-K 2020-10-22]. This indicates stronger demand for bars and structural steel amid weakness in sheet and plate markets.

10. **Steel product shipments to outside customers increased 14% sequentially and were flat year-over-year, supported by resilient nonresidential construction**  
    Shipments of downstream steel products to external customers rose 14% from 2020Q2 and remained flat versus 2019Q3 [8-K 2020-10-22]. Joist and piling products showed double-digit shipment growth year-over-year (+15% and +16%, respectively), while cold finished steel and other steel products declined [8-K 2020-10-22].

11. **Raw materials segment sales and shipments declined 10% in 2020Q3 year-over-year but earnings improved due to better DRI facility margins**  
    Raw materials sales to external customers were \$347 million in 2020Q3, down 13% from 2019Q3, with shipments falling 10% [8-K 2020-10-22; 10-Q 2020-11-12]. Earnings turned positive due to improved pricing and operational performance at DRI plants, partially offset by margin contraction in scrap brokerage [10-Q 2020-11-12].

12. **Pre-operating and start-up costs for new facilities declined to \$22 million in 2020Q3 from \$28 million in 2019Q3, reflecting progress on expansions and new mills**  
    Costs related to facilities under construction or ramp-up, including bar mills in Florida and Illinois, plate mill in Kentucky, and sheet mill expansions, decreased as projects advanced toward full utilization [10-Q 2020-11-12].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

13. **Pricing momentum in sheet and plate markets expected to improve earnings in 2020Q4, despite ongoing COVID-19 uncertainty**  
    Management expects higher earnings in 2020Q4 compared with 2020Q3, driven primarily by improved pricing in sheet and plate mills and better margins at DRI facilities [8-K 2020-10-22; 10-Q 2020-11-12]. This outlook is tempered by the unpredictable impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on demand [8-K 2020-10-22].

### Corporate and Risk Insights

14. **Nucor recorded a \$16.4 million restructuring charge in 2020Q3 related to realignment of its metal buildings business**  
    This charge affected earnings per diluted share by \$0.04 and reflects ongoing efforts to optimize the steel products segment [8-K 2020-10-22; 10-Q 2020-11-12].

15. **An impairment loss of \$299.5 million was recognized in 2020YTD on equity investment in Duferdofin Nucor due to adverse joint venture outlook worsened by COVID-19**  
    This non-cash loss affected consolidated earnings and reflects deteriorated commercial prospects in the joint venture [10-Q 2020-11-12].

16. **Market risk exposures include scrap steel prices, natural gas, and foreign currency; hedging activities mitigate but do not eliminate these risks**  
    Scrap prices decreased modestly in 2020Q3 but remain volatile; natural gas exposure is partially offset by Nucor’s own natural gas production and derivative hedges [10-Q 2020-11-12]. Foreign currency risk is limited and derivative contracts were insignificant at 2020Q3 [10-Q 2020-11-12].

### Wrap Up

Nucor’s 2020Q3 results reflect a partial recovery from the steep earnings and volume declines caused by the COVID-19 pandemic earlier in the year. While shipments and earnings improved sequentially, year-over-year comparisons show significant declines in revenue, earnings, and margins, driven largely by lower steel prices and volume reductions in key product lines like sheet and plate. The steel mills segment showed mixed performance with bars and structural products outperforming sheet and plate, which remain challenged. Nucor’s raw materials segment turned profitable due to better DRI margins despite weaker scrap brokerage. Operating rates rebounded from 2020Q2 lows but remained below 2019 levels. Capital spending was carefully managed with selective reacceleration on major projects, supported by strong liquidity and new bond issuances. Management anticipates further earnings improvement in 2020Q4, contingent on pricing gains in sheet and plate markets amid ongoing pandemic-related uncertainties.

**Guidance overview:** For the fourth quarter of 2020, Nucor expects higher earnings than in 2020Q3, primarily due to improved pricing in sheet and plate mills and better margins at DRI facilities [8-K 2020-10-22; 10-Q 2020-11-12]. The company continues to monitor COVID-19’s impact on demand and supply conditions. No other specific forward-looking financial targets or risk events were disclosed for the near term.

### Wrap Up

Nucor’s 2020Q4 results marked a financial and operational recovery from earlier pandemic-related weakness, with net earnings more than doubling sequentially to \$398.8 million. Steel mill utilization and shipments rebounded in the second half of 2020, supported by a recovering order backlog and improving pricing in key product lines like sheet and plate. Raw material cost volatility persisted, with scrap prices rising late in the year after earlier declines. Nucor’s diversified product mix and vertically integrated raw material supply chain provided operational flexibility amid market uncertainty.

2021.Q4:
### Financial Insights

1. **Nucor set record earnings in 2021Q4 and the full year 2021, with net earnings of \$2.25 billion and \$6.83 billion, respectively, sharply up from 2020**  
   For the quarter ended December 31, 2021, Nucor reported consolidated net earnings of \$2.25 billion, or \$7.97 per diluted share, compared with \$398.8 million, or \$1.30 per diluted share, in 2020Q4. For the full year 2021, net earnings reached \$6.83 billion, or \$23.16 per diluted share, versus \$721.5 million, or \$2.36 per diluted share, in 2020. Net earnings attributable to Nucor stockholders as a percentage of net sales were 18.7% in 2021 compared to 3.6% in 2020 [8-K 2022-01-27; 10-K 2022-02-28].  
   This record profitability was supported by a roughly 81% increase in consolidated net sales to \$36.48 billion in 2021 from \$20.14 billion in 2020, driven by a 64% increase in average sales price per ton and an 11% increase in total tons shipped to outside customers [8-K 2022-01-27; 10-K 2022-02-28].

2. **Average sales price per ton rose 12% sequentially in 2021Q4 despite an 11% decrease in shipments, sustaining strong revenue and margin performance**  
   In 2021Q4, average sales price per ton increased 12% from 2021Q3 and 99% from 2020Q4, while shipments to outside customers declined 11% sequentially and 1% year-over-year to 6.42 million tons [8-K 2022-01-27]. Total steel mill shipments to outside customers decreased 12% from 2021Q3 and 1% from 2020Q4, reflecting a planned outage at the Kentucky sheet mill and lower volumes generally [8-K 2022-01-27].  
   Despite lower volumes, the steel mills segment earnings in 2021Q4 were comparable to 2021Q3, indicating strong pricing power offsetting volume declines [8-K 2022-01-27].

3. **Gross margin and operating rates remained elevated but operating rates at steel mills declined to 89% in 2021Q4 from 96% in 2021Q3**  
   Operating rates at steel mills decreased to 89% in 2021Q4 from 96% in 2021Q3, partly due to the planned outage in December at the Kentucky sheet mill [8-K 2022-01-27]. For the full year 2021, steel mills operated at 94% utilization, up from 82% in 2020 [8-K 2022-01-27; 10-K 2022-02-28].  
   Gross margin for the full year 2021 was \$11.93 billion (sum of quarterly gross margins), reflecting strong metal margins driven by price increases that outpaced raw material cost inflation [10-K 2022-02-28].

4. **Raw materials costs per gross ton increased 67% year-over-year but declined slightly sequentially, pressuring margins in the raw materials segment**  
   The average scrap and scrap substitute cost per gross ton used was \$508 in 2021Q4, down 1% from \$511 in 2021Q3 but up 67% from \$305 in 2020Q4. For the full year 2021, this average cost was \$469, a 62% increase from \$290 in 2020 [8-K 2022-01-27].  
   This raw material inflation contributed to margin compression in the raw materials segment, particularly at the direct reduced iron (DRI) facilities, which led to decreased earnings in 2021Q4 compared to 2021Q3 [8-K 2022-01-27].

5. **Nucor generated strong operating cash flow of \$6.23 billion in 2021, enabling \$3.76 billion in capital returned to shareholders and substantial capital expenditures**  
   Cash provided by operating activities was \$6.23 billion in 2021, up from \$2.70 billion in 2020 [8-K 2022-01-27]. During 2021, Nucor returned approximately \$3.76 billion to stockholders via share repurchases and dividends [8-K 2022-01-27].  
   Capital expenditures for 2021 were approximately \$1.70 billion, focused on growth projects including a plate mill in Kentucky and expansions at Gallatin and Arkansas facilities [10-Q 2021-11-10]. Pre-operating and start-up costs related to these growth projects totaled approximately \$54 million in 2021Q4 and \$130 million for the full year [8-K 2022-01-27].

6. **Nucor maintained a strong liquidity position with \$2.76 billion in cash and equivalents and an undrawn \$1.75 billion revolving credit facility at year-end 2021**  
   At December 31, 2021, cash, short-term investments, and restricted cash totaled \$2.76 billion [8-K 2022-01-27]. The \$1.75 billion revolving credit facility remained undrawn and matures in November 2026 [8-K 2022-01-27].  
   Nucor has the strongest credit rating in the North American steel sector (Baa1/A-) with stable outlooks from Moody’s and S&P [8-K 2022-01-27].

### Operations Insights

7. **Steel mills segment shipments to outside customers declined 1% year-over-year in 2021Q4 but increased 12% for full year 2021, with a mixed product shipment profile**  
   In 2021Q4, steel mills shipped 4.61 million tons to outside customers, down 1% from 2020Q4 [8-K 2022-01-27]. Year-to-date 2021 shipments were 20.30 million tons, up 12% from 18.05 million tons in 2020 [10-K 2022-02-28].  
   Shipments by product in 2021Q4 versus 2020Q4 showed a 6% decline in sheet steel, 5% increase in bars, 19% increase in structural, and 1% increase in plate [8-K 2022-01-27]. Internal steel mill shipments accounted for 22% of total steel mill shipments in 2021Q4, slightly up from 19% in 2020Q4 [8-K 2022-01-27].

8. **Downstream steel product shipments to outside customers decreased 12% sequentially and 1% year-over-year in 2021Q4, but demand in nonresidential construction remained strong**  
   Steel products segment shipments to outside customers declined 12% from 2021Q3 and 1% from 2020Q4 [8-K 2022-01-27]. Despite this, the steel products segment generated increased earnings in 2021Q4 due to strong demand in nonresidential construction markets [8-K 2022-01-27].  
   Notably, shipments of joist, deck, and cold finished steel products increased year-over-year, while piling and tubular products shipments declined [8-K 2022-01-27].

9. **Operating rates at steel mills declined to 89% in 2021Q4 from 96% in 2021Q3, reflecting a planned outage at the Kentucky sheet mill and some volume moderation**  
   The planned outage in December 2021 at the Kentucky sheet mill contributed to the sequential decline in operating rates [8-K 2022-01-27]. Full year 2021 utilization was 94%, up from 82% in 2020 [8-K 2022-01-27].  
   This decline in utilization partially explains the 11% sequential decrease in shipments in 2021Q4 [8-K 2022-01-27].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

10. **Nucor continued to shift towards value-added products and expanded its product portfolio through acquisitions and capital projects**  
    In 2021, Nucor invested approximately \$6.34 billion over three years to expand value-added steel mill products and capabilities, including a \$1 billion acquisition of the insulated metal panel (IMP) business of Cornerstone in August 2021 [10-K 2022-02-28].  
    The IMP business, including brands CENTRIA and Metl-Span, broadens Nucor’s solutions for growing end markets such as warehouses, data centers, and renewable energy [10-K 2022-02-28].  
    Capital projects underway include a \$1.7 billion plate mill in Brandenburg, Kentucky, expected to start production in late 2022 with approximately 1.2 million tons annual capacity [10-K 2022-02-28].

11. **Average sales price per ton increased sharply year-over-year and sequentially, driven by strong market demand and elevated backlogs**  
    Average sales price per ton was \$1,292 in 2021, up 64% from \$789 in 2020 [10-K 2022-02-28]. In 2021Q4, average sales price per ton was 12% higher than 2021Q3 and 99% higher than 2020Q4 [8-K 2022-01-27].  
    Management reported elevated backlogs in both steel mills and steel products segments at year-end 2021 compared to historical levels, supporting pricing [8-K 2022-01-27; 10-K 2022-02-28].

### Corporate and Risk Insights

12. **Nucor identified global steel production overcapacity and import circumvention as ongoing risks to the industry and company profitability**  
    The OECD estimates global steel production overcapacity at approximately 500 million tons, with China’s production near record levels (1.13 billion tons in 2021) [10-K 2022-02-28].  
    Circumvention of trade duties, including production capacity shifts to Southeast Asia, poses a risk to domestic steel pricing and margins [10-K 2022-02-28].  
    Nucor also noted risks from regulatory changes affecting environmental compliance and energy costs, as well as the cyclical nature of the steel industry [8-K 2022-01-27].

### Wrap Up

Nucor delivered record earnings in 2021Q4 and for the full year 2021, driven by strong pricing gains that outpaced raw material cost inflation despite some volume softness and a planned mill outage. Steel mill utilization declined in the final quarter but remained historically high for the year, supporting robust metal margins. The raw materials segment faced margin compression due to elevated scrap and iron ore costs, though overall cash flow generation remained strong, enabling substantial capital returns to shareholders alongside ongoing investments in growth projects and acquisitions focused on value-added products.

Elevated order backlogs and strong demand in nonresidential construction underpinned pricing strength, while the company highlighted ongoing risks from global steel overcapacity and import circumvention. Nucor’s balance sheet remained solid with ample liquidity and no near-term debt maturities. The company projects a slight earnings decline in 2022Q1 relative to the record 2021Q4 but expects continued strong profitability supported by its strategic investments and market position.

**Guidance overview:** For 2022Q1, Nucor expects slightly reduced consolidated net earnings compared to 2021Q4, with diluted EPS benefiting from fewer shares outstanding. The steel mills segment is expected to see lower profitability due to sheet mill performance, while the steel products segment aims for further margin expansion reflecting improved backlog pricing. Raw materials segment earnings are projected to improve slightly due to better DRI facility performance, partially offset by lower scrap prices affecting brokerage operations [8-K 2022-01-27].
